name: 6-pa
title: PA — Physical architecture
subtitle: The components that will be built: behaviour parts hosted in node parts, physical links that are typed, and the budgets the design must hold.

steps.label: SHOW ONLY THE PA LAYER
steps.text: In the Explorer, ⊞ on PA scopes every diagram to the physical-architecture package: the components that will be built.

steps.label: GENERAL VIEW
steps.text: PA's definitions and usages as boxes: node parts and the behaviour they host, the functions carried over from LA, states, hazards, budgets. Too many to read whole.

steps.label: READ ONE ELEMENT
steps.text: Select fleet: the twelve identical drones, multiplicity 12 in Properties. 14 of PA's 21 functions are allocated to it; the ground nodes take the rest.

steps.label: INTERCONNECTION VIEW
steps.text: PA's centrepiece: parts with ports, joined by typed physical links. A node part draws the behaviour parts it hosts nested inside its box.

steps.label: THE GROUND LINKS
steps.text: The ground station, the recall transmitter and the fleet, port to port. Each line is a connection: taskingFeed, priorityFeed, recallBroadcastFeed…

steps.label: A LINK IS TYPED
steps.text: Select recallBroadcastFeed in the Explorer. Properties › Types: RecallRadioMedium, a recall radio separate from the mesh and the ground link.

steps.label: BEHAVIOUR NESTED IN A NODE
steps.text: Select MissionComputerNode and press Selection. The drone's mission computer hosts four behaviour parts: perception, swarmCoordination, reportHold, directiveUptake.

steps.label: HOST A PART IN ITS NODE
steps.text: Before recording we deleted ruleMonitor, the flight-rule monitor that SafetyMonitorNode hosts. Select that node: its box is now empty.

steps.label: PLACE A PART INSIDE IT
steps.text: Pick Part in the palette, then click ON the SafetyMonitorNode box. The part is created inside it and the box is redrawn as its host; Selection frames it.

steps.label: NAME IT AND TYPE IT
steps.text: In Properties: the name ruleMonitor, then the type FlightRuleMonitor, and Enter binds it. That is all the original had: no documentation of its own.

steps.label: THE RESULT
steps.text: The breadcrumb reads PA › SafetyMonitorNode › ruleMonitor, as before we deleted it: the flight rules run apart from the mission computer. Edits stay in this browser.

steps.label: ACTION VIEW
steps.text: The 21 functions carried over from LA, each allocated to a component. No successions and no flows between them: a set, not a sequence.

steps.label: STATE VIEW
steps.text: Five state machines: a drone's sortie and its operating condition, the ground station's link and duty, the fleet's mesh. The sortie one runs on the safety monitor.

steps.label: REQUIREMENT VIEW
steps.text: The six hazards this physical split adds, each satisfied by a component: fleet, the ground station, the recall transmitter, triage, the record store.

steps.label: PARAMETRIC VIEW
steps.text: 15 constraints: the budgets and two checks on estimates, each with its condition in the box. Select one and zoom in: fleetMemberCount ≤ 12, the fleet is not larger than the twelve the brief fixes.

steps.label: TREE VIEW
steps.text: What PA contains, one branch at a time. +N on a box opens what it owns: +4 on MissionComputerNode shows its four behaviour parts.

outro.title: EPBS — End-product breakdown
outro.text: One configuration item per thing procured, built or delivered, each with its contract and its verification. The live model: cosmindxu.github.io/mbse-workflow
